annotation.title_clean: Use of AI in proceedings before the Trademarks Opposition Board
annotation.title_en: Use of AI in proceedings before the Trademarks Opposition Board
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Canadian Intellectual Property Office, Trademarks Opposition Board (ISED)
annotation.venue: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (CIPO website)
annotation.summary_en: Practice notice from Canada's Trademarks Opposition Board requiring parties to declare in the first paragraph of a filing when generative AI was used to create content, and to confirm human verification of content and cited authorities. Failure or false declaration may lead to costs. Clarifies which documents require a declaration.
key_provisions_or_claims: Parties must include a prescribed AI-use declaration in the first paragraph of documents containing generative AI content.
Declaration confirms the party or trademark agent verified AI content and authenticity of cited authorities.
Failure to declare or a false declaration may be unreasonable conduct leading to costs.
Declaration needed for AI-drafted submissions and AI-selected legal authorities or state-of-register evidence; not for objective database searches, editing or speech-to-text tools.
TMOB states it does not currently use AI to render decisions or analyze evidence.
